summary: Frontend E2E test on web preview (390x844) using 2-3 real browser contexts (maya A, leo B, maya C), plus Mongo/API checks. PASS: live WebSocket delivery A->B and B->A in about 0.8s with no reload; typing indicator 'Maya is typing…'; '· Read' on the sender's last message; reciprocal receipts toggle (with leo OFF, neither side sees typing or Read while messages still arrive live; with it back ON, both work again); encrypted photo (decrypted image renders on both sides with the 'Encrypted photo' caption; the stored object has no image magic bytes; the record is in db.chat_media); view-once ('Tap to open' -> viewer -> 'Opened' on both sides and still after reload; API returns 410 for the recipient and 403 for the sender); device linking (third context shows device-pending-panel with a 6-digit code, chat-device-pending is shown and the composer is read-only; A approves -> C is active in about 2.5s; C's chat shows the pre-link messages from both maya and leo (history sync); leo's new message reaches both maya devices and C's message reaches leo and A); takeover; auth guard on signed-out deep links (/settings, /chat -> /welcome). BUGS: (1) REGRESSION: auto-logout after a remote password change now ends on /welcome instead of /auth/login with the red notice (AuthGuard race); (2) settings-signal-status says 'Active on this device' while the device is still pending; (3) takeover leaves other PENDING devices and their sessions alive; (4) stale pending devices look identical in the devices list, so you can't tell which one to approve. Password reset pre-fill was not re-tested.

minor.issue: Only revokes devices with active=True. Other pending devices (e.g. from an abandoned or attacker login) stay pending and their session_jti is not revoked, although the UI promises 'Your other devices are removed'. Seen in DB: maya device 6ae14f313c4587fda152a0a4 stayed pending after 3 takeovers. server.py:1379-1381
Stale comment: says 'One active Signal device per account (deviceId 1)', but this is now multi-device.

ui_bugs.issue: The status text depends only on signalStatus==='ready'. A pending, unlinked device shows 'Active on this device. Keys never leave it.' even though device-pending-panel is shown and the chat composer is disabled. It should read something like 'Waiting for approval from your other device' when useLinkState()==='pending'.

REGRESSION from the new auth guard. After a password change in another session, the 401 handler navigates to /auth/login, but AuthGuard's effect then runs with stale segments ('(tabs)') and user=null, and replaces the route with /welcome. Observed navigation: /chats -> /auth/login -> /welcome. The red notice only appears if the user also taps 'I already have an account'.

issues: Pending devices show only 'web · Waiting for approval', with no creation time or browser/OS. When stale pending entries exist (2 were listed during the test), the user can't tell which one matches the new device. Show the time created (e.g. 'Requested 2 min ago') and hide entries that have expired (link_expires).
The code input is only about 90px wide and its label 'Code shown on the new device' wraps onto 3 lines next to it, which looks cramped. Put the label on its own line and make the input full width.

design_issues.screen: Chat header on a freshly linked device
issues: Right after linking, C's header showed 'Secure session not set up yet' even though history was readable and sending worked. Minor and possibly transient.

action_items: Fix the AuthGuard vs 401-handler race: in AuthGuard, redirect to /auth/login when a login notice is pending (add a peekLoginNotice() to auth-notice.ts), or skip the guard while the unauthorized handler is navigating.
settings.tsx:212: show the pending/unlinked state in settings-signal-status when linkState==='pending'.
POST /signal/takeover: also revoke pending devices (pending=True) belonging to the user and revoke their session_jti.
Devices sheet: show the created time for pending devices, filter out expired pending entries, and give the code input a full-width layout.
photo-bubble.tsx:40-42: any error while opening a view-once photo (including network errors) calls onViewOnceOpened(), which wipes the key locally. Only do that when the server returns 410 or 403.
Optional: live.ts sendTyping uses one global 2.5s throttle across all matches; make it per match.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1814 lines (it was 1565). Split it into routers: auth, signal/devices, media, matches, admin, ws.
chat/[matchId].tsx is 552 lines and close to the 700-line limit. Consider moving the photo send and live-event logic into hooks.
openEncryptedPhoto always labels the decrypted data URI as image/jpeg, even for PNG. Browsers sniff the type so it works, but it's better to store the MIME type inside the encrypted payload.
Revocation over the WebSocket is only checked on the next frame (25s ping), so a revoked session keeps receiving live events until then. Acceptable but worth noting.
Deprecated packages: none found (no expo-av, expo-barcode-scanner or expo-background-fetch).

success_rate.frontend: ~90% (all 6 requested feature flows pass; 1 regression in the auto-logout redirect; status-text bug)

seed_data_creation: Added TEST_ messages, 2 normal and 2 view-once chat_media records to match 6ae148878ee7eecde617a089. Several maya/leo signal_devices records were created (takeovers and one linked device). leo's receipts were restored to ON. ethan's password was changed and reverted to ByteTalks123! (twice, verified 200).
context_for_next_testing_agent: settings-signal-status shows 'Active' even when pending, so ALWAYS open settings-devices-row and check device-pending-panel, then use takeover-password/takeover-submit. When approving from A, stale pending devices may also be listed. Record the device-code-* ids BEFORE the new context logs in and approve the new id. The photo-send sheet animates, so wait about 1.2s before tapping photo-send-normal/view-once (otherwise you get 'outside of viewport'). expo-image-picker on web: use page.expect_file_chooser() around the chat-photo-button tap. subprocess calls to ui_helpers.py work from inside browser scripts.
rca_of_issue: Auto-logout regression: signOut() calls setUser(null). The 401 handler's .finally then calls router.replace('/auth/login'). AuthGuard's useEffect([user, first]) fires for the render with user=null while segments[0] is still '(tabs)', so it calls router.replace('/welcome') after the login navigation. Reproduce: log in as ethan, change the password via API (ui_helpers.py change_pw), tap tab-chats -> URL ends at /welcome. Status-text bug: settings.tsx renders text from useSignalStatus() only and ignores useLinkState().
